title: Why Is Fermi Inc. (FRMI) Stock Down -16.26% Today?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
# Key Takeaways

* **FRMI** shares plunged 16.26% in Friday's session, falling to $6.13 from a prior close of $7.32, as investors reacted to a dilutive convertible notes offering priced after Thursday's close.
* The primary catalyst is the pricing of an upsized $375 million convertible senior notes offering due 2031, which raised concerns about shareholder dilution and the company's ongoing need for external capital.
* Secondary pressure stems from the mechanics of capped call hedging, where counterparties may short shares to establish delta-neutral positions, adding near-term selling pressure.
* The broader pre-revenue energy infrastructure sector remains under scrutiny, and Fermi's ongoing governance disputes with its former CEO continue to weigh on sentiment.
* Traders are now watching for any tenant or joint-venture announcements, the appointment of a permanent CEO, and the company's next quarterly filing for updated cash-burn metrics.

# Opening Summary

Fermi Inc. ([FRMI](https://tickeron.com/ticker/FRMI/)), the Texas-based developer of next-generation private electric grids designed to power hyperscale AI computing, saw its shares tumble 16.26% on Friday. The stock traded at $6.13 as of mid-afternoon, down sharply from Thursday's closing price of $7.32. The sell-off was triggered by the company's announcement late Thursday that it had priced an upsized $375 million convertible senior notes offering, a move that reignited investor concerns about dilution, capital needs, and the pre-revenue company's path to commercial viability.

# Convertible Notes Offering Fuels the Sell-Off

The immediate trigger for Friday's decline was Fermi's pricing of a $375 million convertible senior notes offering due 2031, upsized from an initially proposed $350 million. The notes carry a 5.00% annual coupon and an initial conversion price of approximately $9.52 per share, representing a 30% premium to Thursday's close. While the company also entered into capped call transactions that raise the effective dilution threshold to $14.64 per share, the market focused on the negative implications: the addition of $375 million in senior unsecured debt to a balance sheet that already carried roughly $439 million in total indebtedness as of March 31, 2026, and the potential for future equity dilution if the stock recovers above the conversion price.

Convertible note offerings frequently pressure a stock in the near term for several reasons. First, the option counterparties that sell the capped calls typically hedge their exposure by shorting the underlying stock, creating immediate selling pressure. Second, the very act of raising capital through a convertible structure can signal to the market that a company's cash position requires reinforcement. Fermi disclosed that as of June 30, 2026, it held just $92.0 million in cash and cash equivalents, of which $29.2 million was restricted, underscoring the liquidity imperative behind the offering.

# Governance Overhang and Pre-Revenue Risk

Beyond the mechanics of the convertible offering, [FRMI](https://tickeron.com/ticker/FRMI/) continues to navigate a complex governance landscape. Former CEO and co-founder Toby Neugebauer, who was terminated for cause in April 2026, recently suspended a proxy campaign to call a special shareholder meeting after failing to secure sufficient support. While the company declared the proxy fight "over" on July 7, the underlying litigation between Neugebauer and the company remains active in Texas business court. The ongoing legal battle creates uncertainty around board composition and strategic direction, and the company's own SEC filings warn that these disputes could "adversely affect our business, operating results and financial condition."

Compounding the governance overhang is Fermi's pre-revenue status. The company has yet to sign a binding tenant agreement for its flagship Project Matador campus in Amarillo, Texas, though management has stated it is in advanced negotiations with select counterparties and expects to announce a deal in the third quarter of 2026. Until a tenant is secured, investors are being asked to fund a capital-intensive infrastructure buildout without visibility on the revenue stream that will ultimately service the growing debt load.

# Market Context and Trading Activity

Friday's sell-off occurred on elevated volume, consistent with a market-wide repricing of the stock following the convertible note announcement. The decline pushed [FRMI](https://tickeron.com/ticker/FRMI/) well below its 20-day and 50-day moving averages, and the stock is now trading at levels not seen since mid-June. The move was largely company-specific; broader equity indices were modestly positive during the session, and specialty REIT peers did not exhibit similar weakness, confirming that the convertible offering—not sector or macro forces—drove the price action.

Short interest in [FRMI](https://tickeron.com/ticker/FRMI/) stood at approximately 11.5% of the float as of mid-June, a moderately elevated level that can amplify downward moves when negative catalysts emerge. The hedging activity associated with the convertible notes may have added to the selling pressure, as option counterparties established short positions to offset their exposure under the capped call agreements.

# What Comes Next for FRMI

The path forward for [FRMI](https://tickeron.com/ticker/FRMI/) hinges on several near-term milestones. The company has guided that it expects to sign its first binding joint-venture partner or tenant agreement in the third quarter of 2026, an announcement that would represent a significant de-risking event for the stock. Additionally, Fermi is in advanced discussions to hire a permanent CEO, a move that could help stabilize the leadership vacuum created by Neugebauer's departure and reassure both tenants and financing partners.

On the financial front, the convertible notes are expected to close on July 14, 2026, providing approximately $362 million in net proceeds. How quickly and effectively the company deploys that capital toward turbine installation, site development, and permitting will be closely watched. The company's next earnings report, estimated for August 11, 2026, will offer a critical update on cash burn, construction progress, and any commercial developments. Risks remain substantial: failure to secure a tenant, further governance disruptions, cost overruns on Project Matador, or an inability to access additional capital could all pressure the stock further. Conversely, a credible tenant announcement or progress toward the Department of Energy's Energy Dominance Financing program could shift sentiment rapidly.
